nativeMessaging: Talks to the local companion program that the user's coding agent starts, so routines and recorded runs reach the agent and the agent can drive the browser. Nothing is sent over the network by this.
tabs: Opens, switches and reads the address and title of tabs, so a routine can run in the tab it was started for and the panel can show which site it is on.
scripting: Injects the content script into pages that were open before the extension loaded, so recording and replay work without a reload.
storage: Keeps settings, the list of recent runs and the signed-in session on this device.
identity: Runs the Google sign-in window. Sign-in is optional and is only used to tie routines to an account.
sidePanel: Shows the Agentic Routines panel: the saved routines, what the agent has recorded, and the replay controls where the person approves a paused step.
webNavigation: Lists the frames in a tab, so an agent can read and act inside an embedded form or editor the same way a person does, and leave out frames a person cannot see.
webRequest: Reads which address a page was really loaded from, only while a tab is in a session the user limited to named sites, so that a listed site that turns out to live on a private address is left at once. Nothing is changed or blocked through this permission and nothing is sent anywhere.
declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess: Stops a tab in a session the user limited to named sites from going to any other site, including through a redirect. Each rule covers one tab and is removed when the session lets go of it.
alarms: Wakes the extension about once a minute to reconnect to the user's agent on another computer, only after the user connected one in Settings. A socket alone does not wake a service worker.
downloads: Lets an agent see what the browser downloaded while it was working and get the file, when the user asks it to work with one. It sees nothing from before that agent started.
notifications: Tells the person when an agent hands them a tab for a login, a code or a payment, if they keep that setting on. Clicking it goes to the tab.
offscreen: Makes a video from pictures of a tab, when the person or their agent asks to record it. A service worker has no canvas to do that on. The video is written to a folder on this computer and sent nowhere.
tabGroups: Puts the tab an agent is working in into a group named for that agent, so the person can see which tabs are in use and by whom. The tab leaves the group when the agent is done. Tabs already in one of the person's own groups are left alone.
debugger: Used for things a normal extension cannot do: send clicks, typing and key presses the page treats as a person's, which many sites require, set a local file on a page's file input (uploads), take a screenshot of a tab that is behind another or a window on a hidden desktop, click and type in a tab that is not in front without switching the person to it, and draw one frame in a window that has stopped drawing. It is attached to a tab only while a routine or an agent is driving that tab, and detached a minute after the last action or when the agent's session ends. The browser shows its bar for that whole time, and pressing Cancel on it stops this for ten minutes.
<all_urls>: The user's coding agent works on whichever sites the user asks it to, and routines are replayed on those sites, so the extension cannot list them ahead of time. It acts only on the tab the agent is working in.
